explain.say: Every year on the sixteenth of June, people in Dublin dress in Edwardian clothes and eat kidneys for breakfast. They are celebrating Bloomsday, the day in 1904 when James Joyce set Ulysses, published in Paris in 1922. The timeline follows one ordinary man, Leopold Bloom, through one ordinary day.

explain.say: Why the title? Ulysses is the Latin name for Odysseus, Homer's hero. On the left, the Greek epic; on the right, Joyce's version. Odysseus spends ten years sailing home; Bloom wanders Dublin for a day. Young Stephen Dedalus plays the son, and Molly the wife. Why turn a hero's epic into an ordinary man's day?

Look at five in the afternoon. In a pub, a loud nationalist called the Citizen insults Bloom for being Jewish and hurls a biscuit tin after him. Joyce matches him to Homer's one-eyed giant, the Cyclops. Bloom answers with talk of love, not hate. A gentle note: the scene shows antisemitism. What makes Bloom heroic here?

explain.say: Joyce also rewrites the novel itself. Look at the board: each of the eighteen episodes has its own style. One is broken up by newspaper headlines, one is built like a piece of music, one copies romantic magazine prose, and one is all questions and answers. Why might a writer refuse to keep one voice?

faq.a: The sixteenth of June, the day in 1904 on which Ulysses is set, celebrated every year in Dublin and around the world with readings, costumes and breakfast of kidneys. Joyce chose the date of his first outing with Nora Barnacle.

faq.q: How is Ulysses like the Odyssey?
faq.a: Its eighteen episodes loosely match episodes of Homer's epic: Bloom is Odysseus, Stephen Dedalus is his son Telemachus, and Molly is Penelope, though unfaithful. The parallels make an ordinary day heroic and comic at once.

Its frank treatment of sex and the body was judged obscene. Instalments in the American Little Review were prosecuted in 1921, and copies were seized and burned until Judge John Woolsey cleared it in the United States in 1933.
asks: Was Ulysses banned in the US?

faq.q: What happens in the Cyclops episode?
faq.a: In Barney Kiernan's pub a fierce nationalist called the Citizen picks a fight with Bloom, mocking him as a Jew. Bloom defends love and tolerance, and the Citizen throws a biscuit tin after his departing car.
With Penelope, Molly Bloom's long unpunctuated monologue as she lies in bed, remembering her life and Bloom's proposal, ending with a repeated, affirming yes.

facts: Ulysses was published in Paris on 2 February 1922, Joyce's fortieth birthday, by Sylvia Beach's bookshop Shakespeare and Company.
The novel is set on 16 June 1904 in Dublin.
It has eighteen episodes, each loosely matched to part of Homer's Odyssey.
